nl.statement: Independent and identically distributed sampling: a sample \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) of \(n\) units drawn independently from one fixed observed-data law \(P\), and expectation \(E_P\) taken under that law. — Exact fit: `Causalean.Stat.IIDSample Omega X mu P` bundles Z : N -> Omega -> X, per-index measurability, `iIndepFun`, `IdentDistrib` against Z 0, and `mu.map (Z 0) = P` -- precisely ass:iid-sampling's content. Signature confirmed in Causalean/Stat/Sample.lean:44-50 (namespace Causalean.Stat). Its `sampleMean` / `sampleVariance` API (Concentration/TailBounds/{Bernstein,EmpiricalBernstein}) is what def:cross-fitted-estimator's n^{-1} sums and V-hat will be phrased against, and `Causalean.Stat.KFoldSplit` (Stat/SampleSplit/KFold.lean, namespace Causalean.Stat) supplies the two-fold split plus `KFoldSplit.folds_indep` (evaluation fold independent of its training complement) used for the cross-fit conditioning in thm:uniform-endpoint-efficiency. The observation type X is instantiated at the S2 observed unit.

A quadratic-endpoint censored-survival experiment on the unit square. A unit carries a covariate \(X\in[0,1]\) with Lebesgue density \(f\), a binary treatment \(A\in\{0,1\}\) with propensity \(\pi_1(x)=P(A=1\mid X=x)\) and \(\pi_a(x)=a\pi_1(x)+(1-a)\{1-\pi_1(x)\}\), two potential event times \(T(0),T(1)\in[0,\infty]\) whose conditional hazards are \(\lambda_a(t,x)\) with survivals \(S_a(t\mid x)=\exp\{-\int_0^t\lambda_a(v,x)\,dv\}\), and a censoring time \(C\in[0,1]\) whose conditional survival factors exactly as \(G_a(t\mid x)=(1-t)^2g_a(t,x)\) for \(t<1\) with \(G_a(1\mid x)=0\) and \(g_a(0,x)=1\). The realized event time is \(T=T(A)\); only the coarsened unit \(O=(X,A,U,\Delta)\) with \(U=\min\{T,C\}\in[0,1)\) and \(\Delta=\mathbf 1\{T\le C\}\) is observed. Attached to the observed unit are the counting process \(N(t)=\mathbf 1\{U\le t,\Delta=1\}\), the at-risk process \(Y_{\mathrm{risk}}(t)=\mathbf 1\{U\ge t\}\), the event martingale \(M_a(t)=N(t)-\int_0^tY_{\mathrm{risk}}(v)\lambda_a(v,X)\,dv\) on \(\{A=a\}\), and the rescaled at-risk function \(q_a(t,x)=S_a(t\mid x)g_a(t,x)\). A diagnostic margin \(\delta\in(0,1)\) and the shorter horizon \(\tau=1-\delta\) are fixed constants of the in-class sanity check only. — Define-local. Search trace: grep -i 'RMST|restricted mean survival|Kaplan|Nelson|censor|hazard|at-risk|atRisk' over /Causalean -> 0 files; glob Causalean/{Stat,Estimation,PO}/**; leansearch 'counting process compensator martingale right-censored survival hazard' -> only Mathlib MeasureTheory.Martingale / martingale_nat / martingalePart / predictablePart (abstract discrete-index martingales; no compensator of a counting process, no survival analysis). SUBSTRATE SURVEY RECORD (per the substrate-survey rule): (1) `Causalean.PO.Core.System.POSystem` + `PO.Assumptions.Consistency.POSystem.Consistency` + `PO.Core.Counterfactual` -- BYPASS-JUSTIFIED: regime/Finset-indexed abstract PO skeleton (documented as sorry-bearing) with no coarsening/censoring layer; here the potential outcome is a TIME T(a) and the observed unit is the CENSORED coarsening (X,A,U,Delta), so the plumbing adds no proof leverage to a purely analytic/probabilistic argument. (2) `Causalean.PO.ID.Exact.ATE.POBackdoorSystem` -- BYPASS-JUSTIFIED: requires an OBSERVED real-valued outcome variable Y with `factualY`; here min{T(a),1} is never observed (it is censored), so `hYreal`/`factualY` are unfillable. (3) `Causalean.Estimation.ATE.Setup.BackdoorEstimationSystem` -- BYPASS-JUSTIFIED: its `mu_val : Bool -> gamma -> R` outcome-regression and `mu_reg_compat` tie an observed-outcome adjustment functional, which does not exist under censoring; the nuisance triple here is (pi_1, lambda_a, g_a), not (e, mu). (4) `Causalean.Stat.IIDSample` -- REUSED (S1). Helpers/ObservedLaw.lean derives the two structural identities of `decisions.observed_law_identities_are_world_lemmas` from the latent construction, and M_a is carried only through its closed form (see `decisions.closed_form_martingale_encoding`), never as a stochastic integrator.

The radius-\(20\) isotropic Hölder primitive class and the fixed-horizon RMST target. The norm \(\lVert\cdot\rVert_{C^{3,1}}\) is the maximum of the suprema of derivatives through order three and the Lipschitz seminorms of the third derivatives, and \(\mathcal H^4_{20}(\mathcal X)=\{h:\lVert h\rVert_{C^{3,1}(\mathcal X)}\le20\}\). The primitive class \(\mathcal P_4\) collects the laws satisfying the causal-structural, band, exact-quadratic-censoring and three radius-\(20\) Hölder conditions; \(\mathcal P_4^{\circ}\) is its interior subclass, cut out by positivity of the interior-slack functional \(\rho_{\mathrm{int}}\). The target is the causal restricted-mean contrast \(\theta=\theta_1-\theta_0\) with \(\theta_a=E_P[m_a(X)]\) and \(m_a(x)=\int_0^1S_a(v\mid x)\,dv\); the remaining-life weight is \(H_a(t,x)=S_a(t\mid x)^{-1}\int_t^1S_a(v\mid x)\,dv\), the arm influence component is \(D_a\), the contrast influence function is \(D=D_1-D_0\), and the influence variance is \(V_P=E_P[D(O)^2]\). The law \(P^{\star}\) is the explicit interior witness whose feasible score has a \(5/2\) moment but no third moment. — Define-local wrapper over an EXACT library predicate. `Causalean.Stat.Nonparametric.HolderBallStd f order M S` (Causalean/Stat/Nonparametric/Approximation/HolderInterpolation/Defs.lean:106-112) instantiated at order = 4 unfolds to: ContDiffOn R 3 f S, all iterated derivatives of order <= 3 bounded by M on S, and the order-3 derivative M-Lipschitz on S (exponent 4-3 = 1) -- literally the core's ||.||_{C^{3,1}} <= 20 condition, so H^4_20 = HolderBallStd . 4 20 . with no gap. BOUNDARY READING (round 5, see decisions.boundary_taylor_bridge): the predicate's bound and Lipschitz clauses are phrased with the GLOBAL `iteratedFDeriv` evaluated at points of S, whereas the paper's norm at a boundary point of the closed square is the one-sided (within-S) derivative; the class predicate is kept EXACTLY as the library states it -- the assumption is not strengthened to a global `ContDiff` and the radius 20 is not enlarged -- and Helpers/BoundaryTaylor.lean supplies `holderBallStd_within_of_convex`, which derives the same two bounds for `iteratedFDerivWithin R j . S` at every point of S (interior agreement + continuity of the within-derivative + density of the interior in a convex body). All boundary-cell Taylor work downstream runs through that within-form; no boundary node consumes the global-derivative clause directly. Search trace: grep 'olderBall|IsHolder|holderNorm|HolderClass|holderSeminorm' over /Causalean -> HolderInterpolation{,/Defs}, HolderTaylor, HolderTaylorMonomial only; Mathlib side checked (`HolderWith` / `MemHolder` are exponent-in-(0,1] only, no integer-order ball); Mathlib within-derivative pieces confirmed to exist this round: `iteratedFDerivWithin_of_isOpen`, `iteratedFDerivWithin_congr_set`, `iteratedFDerivWithin_eq_iteratedFDeriv`, `ContDiffOn.continuousOn_iteratedFDerivWithin`, `uniqueDiffOn_convex`, `Convex.closure_interior_eq_closure_of_nonempty_interior`, `ContinuousLinearMap.iteratedFDerivWithin_comp_right`, `iteratedFDerivWithin_comp_add_left'`, `taylor_mean_remainder_lagrange`, `uniqueDiffOn_Icc_zero_one`. rho_int, m_a, theta_a, theta, H_a, D_a, D, V_P are plain interval-integral / expectation defs over S1-S2 (D_a in the closed form of `decisions.closed_form_martingale_encoding`); no Causalean analogue exists because none of them is defined without the censored-survival world.

The two-fold cross-fitted endpoint learner and its Wald inference. On a training sample of size \(M\) the resolution is \(J_M=\max\{1,\lfloor(M/\log(M+2))^{1/12}\rfloor\}\) with bandwidth \(h_M=J_M^{-1}\) and primitive rate \(r_M=h_M^4+\sqrt{\log(M+2)/(Mh_M^4)}+\log(M+2)/(Mh_M^4)\). The learner returns the foldwise nuisance triple \(\widehat\eta=(\widehat\pi_a,\widehat\lambda_a,\widehat g_a)_{a=0,1}\), from which \(\widehat S_a,\widehat G_a,\widehat H_a,\widehat m_a\) are formed by the same formulas as their population counterparts; a generic in-band triple \(\bar\eta=(\bar\pi_a,\bar\lambda_a,\bar g_a)_{a=0,1}\) with derived \(\bar S_a,\bar G_a,\bar H_a,\bar m_a\) is the argument of the integrated one-step score \(\psi_a\). A deterministic fold map \(k:\{1,\ldots,n\}\to\{1,2\}\) assigns each unit its contribution \(W_i\); the total estimator is \(\widehat\theta\) and the nonnegative variance estimator is \(\widehat V\). Inference uses the standard normal distribution function \(\Phi\), a nominal error probability \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), the quantile \(z_{1-\alpha/2}=\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/2)\), and the Wald interval \(\mathcal I_{n,\alpha}\). — Define-local. The fold map k and the -k(i) training rule reuse `Causalean.Stat.KFoldSplit` with K = 2 (fold / trainComplement / fold_disjoint_trainComplement / folds_indep, Causalean/Stat/SampleSplit/KFold.lean:66-86); the n^{-1} sums of theta-hat and V-hat reuse `Causalean.Stat.IIDSample.sampleMean` / `sampleVariance`. Phi reuses Mathlib's `ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal 0 1` via `Causalean.Stat.gaussianMeasure` (Stat/Inference/Studentize.lean), whose no-atom / null-frontier facts (`gaussianMeasure_zero_one_singleton`, `gaussianMeasure_zero_one_frontier_Icc`) are exactly what prop:uniform-wald-coverage's distribution-function sandwich needs. Search trace: grep 'crossFit|CrossFit|cross-fit' over /Causalean -> Estimation/OrthogonalMoments/DMLCrossFit.lean, Stat/EmpiricalProcess/CrossFitRate.lean, Stat/SampleSplit/*; none carries a survival/endpoint learner, and `dmlCrossFitEstimator` is the Chernozhukov J-inverse Z-estimation form rather than a plain one-step mean, so the estimator object itself is local.

The local semiparametric experiment at an interior law. An admissible submodel through \(P\in\mathcal P_4^{\circ}\) is a one-parameter family of observed-data laws \(e\mapsto P_e\) which stays inside \(\mathcal P_4^{\circ}\) for all sufficiently small \(\lvert evert\), satisfies \(P_0=P\), and is differentiable in quadratic mean at \(e=0\): for a common dominating measure \(
u\), \[\int\left\{\sqrt{dP_e/d
u}-\sqrt{dP/d
u}-	frac12e\,s\sqrt{dP/d
u}ight\}^2d
u=o(e^2),\] where the score \(s\in L^2_0(P)\) is by definition the quadratic-mean derivative of that same path. The tangent set at \(P\) is the closed linear span in \(L^2(P)\) of the scores of all such submodels, and the pathwise derivative of \(	heta\) at \(P\) is represented on that closure by the inner product with a gradient. — REVISED (round 4; F2.5 rooted the defect in this S-block). Auxiliary world for thm:canonical-gradient-efficiency only; it binds no new core symbol (every symbol it mentions is bound by S1-S4), so P1's symbol coverage is unaffected. DEFINE-LOCAL in Helpers/Tangent.lean: `structure RmstRegularSubmodel (P : EndpointLaw) (hP : InteriorHolderClass P)` with fields `path : R -> EndpointLaw`, `path_zero : path 0 = P`, `path_mem : exists eps > 0, forall e, |e| < eps -> InteriorHolderClass (path e)` (the in-class law path t |-> P_t), `score : Lp R 2 P.mu`, `score_meanZero`, and `score_spec : IsQmDerivative path score` -- the DQM/L^2-differentiability condition at 0 written WITH `score` as its derivative (the core's (E14)), which is exactly the path<->score tie the library structure lacks; then `def rmstTangentSet P hP : Submodule R (Lp R 2 P.mu) := (Submodule.span R (Set.range (fun m : RmstRegularSubmodel P hP => m.score))).topologicalClosure` (tangent set = closed span of scores of such submodels) and `def IsRmstPathwiseGradient P hP psi g : Prop := forall m : RmstRegularSubmodel P hP, HasDerivAt (fun e => psi (m.path e)) (inner g m.score) 0`. nl.statement:
On a training sample \((O_i)_{i=1}^M\), put \(J=J_M\), \(h=h_M=J^{-1}\), \(I_j=[jh,(j+1)h)\), and \(K_\ell=[\ell h,(\ell+1)h)\) for \(j,\ell\in\{0,\ldots,J-1\}\), assigning \(x=1\) to \(K_{J-1}\); write \(d_j=1-jh\).  Let \(p(z_t,z_x)\) be the fixed vector of the ten monomials of total degree at most three, \(v(z)=(1,z,z^2,z^3)^{\mathsf T}\), \(p_{j\ell}(t,x)=p((t-jh)/h,(x-\ell h)/h)\), and \(v_\ell(x)=v((x-\ell h)/h)\).  Define the known positive constants
\[
 \beta_*:=\lambda_{\min}\!\left\{\int_{[0,1]^2}(1-z_t)^2p(z_t,z_x)p(z_t,z_x)^{\mathsf T}\,dz_t\,dz_x\right\},
 \qquad
 \beta_\pi:=\lambda_{\min}\!\left\{\int_0^1v(z)v(z)^{\mathsf T}\,dz\right\}.
\]
For every arm and time--covariate cell form
\[
 R_{aj\ell}:=\sum_{i=1}^M\mathbf 1\{A_i=a,X_i\in K_\ell\}
 \int_{I_j}Y_{i,\mathrm{risk}}(t)p_{j\ell}(t,X_i)p_{j\ell}(t,X_i)^{\mathsf T}\,dt,
\]
\[
 b_{aj\ell}:=\sum_{i=1}^M\mathbf 1\{A_i=a,X_i\in K_\ell,U_i\in I_j,\Delta_i=1\}p_{j\ell}(U_i,X_i),
\]
\[
 Q_{aj\ell}:=\sum_{i=1}^M\mathbf 1\{A_i=a,X_i\in K_\ell\}
 \int_{I_j}(1-t)^2p_{j\ell}(t,X_i)p_{j\ell}(t,X_i)^{\mathsf T}\,dt,
\]
\[
 c_{aj\ell}:=\sum_{i=1}^M\mathbf 1\{A_i=a,X_i\in K_\ell\}
 \int_{I_j}Y_{i,\mathrm{risk}}(t)p_{j\ell}(t,X_i)\,dt.
\]
Declare the cell successful when
\[
 \lambda_{\min}(R_{aj\ell})\ge e^{-2}\beta_*Mh^2d_j^2/32
 \quad\hbox{and}\quad
 \lambda_{\min}(Q_{aj\ell})\ge\beta_*Mh^2d_j^2/16.
\]
On a successful cell set \(\widehat\gamma_{aj\ell}=R_{aj\ell}^{-1}b_{aj\ell}\), \(\widehat\zeta_{aj\ell}=Q_{aj\ell}^{-1}c_{aj\ell}\),
\[
 \widehat\lambda_a(t,x)=\operatorname{clip}_{[1/2,2]}\{p_{j\ell}(t,x)^{\mathsf T}\widehat\gamma_{aj\ell}\},
 \qquad
 \widehat q_a^{\mathrm{raw}}(t,x)=p_{j\ell}(t,x)^{\mathsf T}\widehat\zeta_{aj\ell}.
\]
If the cell is unsuccessful, set \(\widehat\lambda_a(t,x)=1\) and mark that cell for the residual fallback below.  From the resulting piecewise hazard define
\[
 \widehat S_a(t\mid x):=\exp\!\left\{-\int_0^t\widehat\lambda_a(s,x)\,ds\right\}.
\]
On each successful cell set
\[
 \widehat g_a(t,x)=\operatorname{clip}_{[1/2,2]}\left\{\frac{\widehat q_a^{\mathrm{raw}}(t,x)}{\widehat S_a(t\mid x)}\right\};
\]
on each unsuccessful cell set \(\widehat g_a(t,x)=1\).  Thus \(\widehat G_a(t\mid x)=(1-t)^2\widehat g_a(t,x)\), and define \(\widehat H_a\) and \(\widehat m_a\) from \(\widehat\lambda_a\) by the same integral formulas as \(H_a\) and \(m_a\).

For every covariate cell form
\[
 P_\ell:=\sum_{i=1}^M\mathbf 1\{X_i\in K_\ell\}v_\ell(X_i)v_\ell(X_i)^{\mathsf T},
 \qquad
 s_\ell:=\sum_{i=1}^M\mathbf 1\{X_i\in K_\ell\}v_\ell(X_i)A_i.
\]
If \(\lambda_{\min}(P_\ell)\ge\beta_\pi Mh/4\), set \(\widehat\alpha_\ell=P_\ell^{-1}s_\ell\) and
\[
 \widehat\pi_1(x)=\operatorname{clip}_{[1/4,3/4]}\{v_\ell(x)^{\mathsf T}\widehat\alpha_\ell\},
 \qquad \widehat\pi_0(x)=1-\widehat\pi_1(x);
\]
otherwise set \(\widehat\pi_1(x)=\widehat\pi_0(x)=1/2\) on that cell.  Half-open cells and the stated last-cell convention select a unique formula at every input.  These fixed threshold, clipping, and fallback rules define a Borel-measurable total learner using only the training observations, \(M,h_M\), the fixed bases, and the displayed class constants.

nl.statement:
The answer is affirmative.  The local-cubic handle in def:endpoint-learning-handle has a measurable total completion for which there are constants \(C,c>0\), depending only on the displayed class constants and the fixed polynomial bases, such that for all sufficiently large \(M\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_4}P\!\left(
 \max_{a\in\{0,1\}}\lVert\widehat\lambda_a-\lambda_a\rVert_\infty+
 \max_{a\in\{0,1\}}\lVert\widehat g_a-g_a\rVert_\infty+
 \lVert\widehat\pi_1-\pi_1\rVert_\infty>C r_M\right)
 \le C M^{-2}+C J_M^2\exp(-cMh_M^3).
\]
In particular, \(r_M=O\{(\log M/M)^{1/3}\}\), uniformly over the arbitrary measurable covariate densities allowed by \(\mathcal P_4\).

nl.statement: At \(P\in\mathcal P_4^{\circ}\), suppose the finite-dimensional local experiments generated by finite collections of scores from the tangent score space are locally asymptotically normal, and suppose an estimator sequence is regular relative to all those experiments. If \(\theta\) is pathwise differentiable with canonical gradient \(D\) in the closure of that score space, then every weak limit law of the centered estimator sequence is the convolution of \(N(0,E_P[D(O)^2])\) and another probability law. In particular, whenever its asymptotic variance exists, it is at least \(V_P=E_P[D(O)^2]\).

review.note: Lean self-containedly encodes LAN for all finite tangent-score experiments, estimator regularity for those experiments, canonical-gradient membership in the tangent closure, convolution of every centered subsequential weak limit with the efficient Gaussian law, and the equivalent finite-second-moment variance lower bound.
